evidence.quote: Length 96.60 km
UNESCO added the Kalka–Shimla Railway to the mountain railways of India World Heritage Site

SH2.claim: The Ridge and the Mall remain its landmarks, with Viceregal Lodge, Christ Church, Gaiety Theatre and Gorton Castle among its colonial buildings.

evidence.quote: The Ridge and The Mall are still popular landmarks just as they were in the pre-Independence era.
The imperial Viceregal Lodge, the graceful Christ Church, Gaiety Theatre, Gorton Castle, Barnes Court and several buildings are part of the colonial architectural heritage of the town.

SH3.claim: Viceregal Lodge (1888) now houses the Indian Institute of Advanced Study; parts are open to visitors.

evidence.quote: When completed in 1888, the Viceregal Lodge was one of the most flamboyant and one of first electric buildings of India.

evidence.quote: Overlooking the hill station at 2,445 meters altitude, Jakhoo Hill is Shimla city’s acme and home to Lord Hanuman.
The daunting half-an-hour uphill climb from The Ridge finally ends at Jakhoo Temple. Ropeway service to Jakhoo temple is also available.

HD1.claim: The Hadimba Devi Temple was built in 1553 CE by Maharaja Bahadur Singh in the Dhungiri cedar forest.

is the only temple in India in his honour

VA1.claim: Vashisht, about 3 km from Manali across the Beas, is known for its sulphurous hot springs and the Kath Kuni-style temple of Sage Vashisht.

Renowned for its sulphurous hot springs and the ancient Vashisht Temple
the Vashisht Temple is a masterpiece of Kath Kuni architecture

tourist vehicles start making a beeline to the Pass to experience snow in the months of June to August

evidence.quote: The airport at Bhuntar is 50 km from Manali from where taxis and buses are readily available.
Flights are available to and from Delhi, Chandigarh and Jubbar-hatti (Shimla). From Delhi, it takes one & half an hour to reach Kullu-Manali Airport.

MN16.claim: Delhi to Manali is about 550 km by road; deluxe and AC Volvo buses run regularly, and booking ahead is recommended.

evidence.quote: The road journey from Delhi to Manali is about 550 km, and an advance booking of tickets in the AC/Volvo coaches is recommended
Deluxe, semi-deluxe, AC, Volvo buses ply regularly to these places.
Manali is well connected by road with Delhi, Chandigarh, Dehradun, Haridwar, Shimla, Dharamshala and Chamba.

MN25.claim: Vehicles not registered in Himachal pay a green tax to enter Manali — ₹100 for a bike, ₹200 for a car (LMV), ₹300 for a passenger vehicle, ₹500 for a goods vehicle — valid seven days, bought online up to nine days ahead, printout required.

evidence.quote: This tax is paid for every vehicle that is not registered in the State of Himachal Pradesh. The permit is valid for seven days.
Bike 100 2 LMV 200 3 Passenger Vehicle 300 4 Goods Vehicle 500

RO3.claim: Tourist vehicles need an online permit, issued against a daily quota set by the National Green Tribunal and the district; it is valid for one day, can be applied for up to two days ahead, and vehicles must be no more than 10 years old.

evidence.quote: daily quota defined by National Green Tribunal(NGT)/District Administration. The tourism permit is valid for one day only (To & Fro).
Permits can only be applied for next 2 days from the current date.
Vehicle Registration Date (Age of vehicle not to be more than 10 yrs)

RO7.claim: Rohtang permits are capped each day at 800 petrol and 400 diesel vehicles, released online in two batches at 10:00 and 16:00.

(i) 10:00 hrs (200 Diesel and 400 Petrol) (ii) 16:00 hrs (200 Diesel and 400 Petrol)

HS15.claim: Daily flights from Delhi land at Jubbarhatti, 23 km from Shimla.

evidence.quote: There are daily flights from Delhi to Shimla Airport at Jubbarhatti, at a distance of 23 kms from the city.

HP13.claim: In the monsoon (July–August) roads are slippery and landslides and rock-falls happen; drive with care.

evidence.quote: During the monsoon season (July-August), be careful while driving on the road because of slippery conditions and land-slides/ rock-falls.

MN12.claim: Weather changes abruptly — thunderstorms and sudden snowfall can turn a warm day cold in minutes — so woollens are essential, even light ones in summer.

evidence.quote: Thunderstorms and sudden snowfalls do cause a sharp drop in temperature turning an otherwise warm day into a cold one in a matter of minutes. Woolens are essential when visiting Manali.

HP17.claim: Use only government-authorised, licensed agencies for trekking, rafting and paragliding.

evidence.quote: ensure the agencies offering such activities are authorized by the Government for the purpose and have a valid license to operate.

evidence.quote: The route is on NH – 22 (The Hindustan Tibet Road). Buses and Taxis are available at Shimla and Rampur.

Kinner Kailash, abode of Lord Shiva from Kalpa, to the pristine lake at Nako village

AT1.claim: The 9.02-km Atal Tunnel carries NH3 between Manali and Keylong, bypassing Rohtang Pass; it is the world's longest single-tube highway tunnel above 10,000 ft (3,048 m).

is the longest highway single-tube tunnel above 10,000 feet (3,048 m) in the world

HS14.claim: Regular buses run Manali–Kaza from July to October and Shimla–Kinnaur–Kaza from May to October; sturdy off-road taxis are recommended.

evidence.quote: From Manali to Kaza, there are regular buses from July to October and from Shimla via Kinnaur, there are regular buses from May to October.
Sturdy vehicles used as off-roading taxis are recommended for a travel tour to Spiti from Manali or Shimla.

HS21.claim: In Spiti only BSNL mobile works well and internet is slow.

evidence.quote: Owing to its remoteness and high altitude only BSNL mobile phone network works fine in Spiti. Internet speed is slow.

SP8.claim: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Spiti near the Tibet border.

evidence.quote: Foreign tourists require Inner Line Permits to visit certain inner area of Kinnaur district and Spiti of the Lahaul-Spiti district that borders Tibet-China.

HP14.claim: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Kinnaur and Spiti on the Tibet border; permits are issued in New Delhi (Himachal Bhawan), Shimla, Reckong Peo and at SDM offices in Kalpa, Kaza and Manali.

evidence.quote: Foreign tourists require Inner Line Permits to visit certain inner area of Kinnaur district and Spiti of the Lahaul-Spiti district that borders Tibet-China.

The Permits are issued by Resident Commissioner of Himachal Pradesh, Himachal Bhawan, 27, Sikandra Road, New Delhi and at Deputy Commissioner’s office at Shimla, Kinnaur at Reckong Peo and SDM office at Kalpa, Kaza, Manali.

HS13.claim: Spiti is pleasant from April to October (about 15–20°C in May–June) and can fall to −20°C in winter.

evidence.quote: Weather in Spiti is pleasant from April to October, with the May-June temperatures hovering at a comfortable 15°C and 20°C make it a good time to visit the valley.
In winters, the temperature falls to as low as minus 20 degree Celsius.

HS22.claim: Kinnaur has good mobile signal at Reckong Peo, Kalpa and Sangla, but internet can be weak and many trek routes have none.

evidence.quote: Good mobile phone connectivity is available at Reckong Peo, Kalpa, Sangla and other destinations. However, internet connectivity may be low in most other areas. Many trek routes and offbeat destinations may not have any mobile phone connectivity at all.

DS7.claim: Kangra airport at Gaggal is 13–14 km from Dharamshala, with regular flights from Delhi.

evidence.quote: Kangra airport at Gaggal is at a distance of 14 km from Dharamshala. There are regular flights between Delhi and Kangra to this airport.
The nearest Airport is at Gaggal, 13 Kms from Dharamshala and 8 Kms from Kangra Town.

DS28.claim: The Tsuglagkhang temple complex is the centre of McLeodganj, with the market around it.

evidence.quote: Major section of the market is centered around the Tsuglag Khang Temple, bestowing good wishes on residents and tourists.

DS15.claim: The Bhagsunag temple, 2 km from McLeodganj, has a spring-fed pool for a holy dip; the waterfall above is fullest from July to September.

evidence.quote: The spring water flows into a pool where pilgrims do take a holy dip. The temple at a walkable distance is just 2 kms from Mcleodganj.
The best time to be at the waterfall is in the rainy season from July to September when the stream is in full flow.

DS25.claim: Triund (2,875 m) is a moderate trek through oak and deodar forest; the last stretch climbs 22 steep bends to an open camping ground.

evidence.quote: a summer trek to Triund (altitude 2875 meter), just below the snowline
Making way through thick oak and deodar forests with scattered rhododendron flowers in the path, this moderate trek
The last stretches of the trek are demanding as you make your way up the 22 gruelling curves to an open camping ground.

DS14.claim: Dharamkot, above McLeodganj, is home to many foreigners and is the base for the Triund trek.

evidence.quote: Dharamkot is home to many foreigners and life in this small village is influenced by western lifestyles. This village is also the base for a trek to Triund

DS19.claim: Norbulingka Institute at Sidhpur, 7 km from Dharamshala, was founded in 1995 to preserve Tibetan arts, crafts and culture.

evidence.quote: The institute was founded in 1995 by Kelsang and Kim Yeshi to preserve the Tibetan arts, crafts and culture. Norbulingka Institute at Sidhpur is 7 km from Dharamshala.
Streams running through well maintained Japanese styled gardens, birds fluttering about in trees and the vibrant Tibetan architecture of Norbulingka Institute

DL3.claim: The Mall Road is the place for Himachali shawls, Chamba rumals, traditional jewellery and Tibetan handicrafts.

evidence.quote: The Mall Road is a good place to shop for woollen Himachali shawls, Chamba rumals, traditional jewellery, Tibetan handicrafts and other items.

DL17.claim: Dainkund (2,755 m) is the highest hill around Dalhousie; a side road from 13 km along the Khajjiar road leads up.

evidence.quote: Dainkund is the highest mountain among the hills around Dalhousie. From an altitude of 2755 meters the views are wide
a diverting road from an intersection at 13 km from Dalhousie on the road to Khajjiar leads to Diankund peak.

DL14.claim: Khajjiar is a wide meadow around a pond, ringed by cedar forest, with the 12th-century Khajji Nag temple nearby.

evidence.quote: Often compared with Swiss mountain meadows, Khajjiar is a wide grassy clearing around a pond with a thick cedar forest.
A few meters from the pond is the temple of Khajji Nag that dates back to the 12th century AD.

DL15.claim: Khajjiar is 22–23 km from Dalhousie and 24–26 km from Chamba; an easy trek also comes up from Chamba.

evidence.quote: This scenic spot is 24 km from Chamba and 22 km from Dalhousie.
This scenic spot is 26 km from Chamba and 23 km from Dalhousie.
an easy trek to Khajjiar from Chamba brings you up close with nature

CB7.claim: The Chaugan is Chamba's central grassy ground for picnics, sports and festivals, and hosts the Minjar fair.

evidence.quote: The nerve centre of Chamba, Chaugan is a grassy open area, ideal for leisure, picnics and holding of sporting events.
The Chaugan plays host to the annual Minjar Mela.

CB9.claim: The Lakshmi Narayan complex has six shikhara temples; the main one, to Vishnu, was built by the town's founder Raja Sahil Varman.

evidence.quote: consisting of 6 temples is a landmark of the historical town
The main temple, dedicated to Lord Vishnu, was built by Raja Sahil Varman who founded the town.
Interestingly three of these temples are dedicated to Lord Shiva and one to Radha Krishna.
Dalhousie is 54 km from Chamba.

DL4.claim: Pathankot station is 87 km away and Gaggal (Kangra) airport 110 km; buses run to Pathankot, Amritsar, Delhi, Shimla, Chamba and Bharmaur.

evidence.quote: Rail: Nearest train station to Dalhousie is Pathankot, 87 km away.
The nearest domestic airport to Dalhousie is Gaggal Airport ( Kangra) which is 110 km away.
Public and private transport services are available for Pathankot, Amritsar, Delhi, Shimla and other cities. There are regular bus services for Chamba, Bharmaur and other destinations.

DL12.claim: Summer is the best time for Dalhousie and Khajjiar — clear skies from March to June — while winters are cold with heavy snow.

evidence.quote: Summer is the best time to be in Dalhousie and Khajjiar. Spring breaks out in March and till June the skies are usually clear
Winters are cold as the hill stations does receive heavy rounds of snow.

Ensure hiring only Govt. registered guides, porters and from registeredagencies

Easy to reach, this highly revered temple is 15 km for Dharamshala and 24 km from Kangra.

Buses regularly ply to Kasol and taxis are also easily available for hire.

Surrounded by green tea estates and forests of pine and deodar

sections.heading: By air
sections.text: Five airports serve the state: Chandigarh and Pathankot on its borders, and Gaggal-Kangra, Bhuntar-Kullu and Jubbarhatti-Shimla inside it. Gaggal and Pathankot are for Kangra, Dharamshala and Chamba; Bhuntar for Kullu, Manali, Mandi and Lahaul-Spiti; Chandigarh and Jubbarhatti for Shimla, Solan and Kinnaur. Bhuntar has flights to Delhi and Chandigarh; daily flights from Delhi land at Jubbarhatti; Gaggal has regular flights from Delhi.

sections.heading: By train
sections.text: Broad-gauge trains reach Kalka and Pathankot. From Kalka, the 96 km narrow-gauge line to Shimla — opened in 1903 and part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site — is a journey in itself. From Pathankot a narrow-gauge line runs through the Kangra valley to Joginder Nagar, passing Kangra station, 20 km from Dharamshala, and Ahju, 3 km from Bir. There is no railway to Manali.

sections.heading: By bus
sections.text: Interstate buses run from Delhi, Chandigarh, Jaipur and other nearby cities. Ordinary and luxury coaches link Delhi and Chandigarh with Shimla and Kullu, and deluxe and AC Volvo buses run to Manali — booking ahead is recommended. Within the state, public transport and taxis serve every destination.

sections.heading: Spiti and Kinnaur
sections.text: Kinnaur is on NH-22, the Hindustan–Tibet Road, with buses and taxis from Shimla and Rampur. Regular buses reach Kaza from Shimla via Kinnaur between May and October and from Manali only between July and October; sturdy off-road taxis are recommended on both routes.

sections.heading: Driving yourself
sections.text: Cars not registered in Himachal pay a green tax to enter Manali (₹200 for a car, valid seven days). On hill roads keep to the left, don't overtake on bends and slow down at corners, and in July–August expect slippery roads and landslides.

sections.heading: Atal Tunnel instead of Rohtang
sections.text: The 9.02 km Atal Tunnel needs no Rohtang permit. The route through it to Lahaul is 71 km and about 2 hours, against 116 km and 5–6 hours over the pass. Sissu's panchayat has at times paused tourist activities, so check locally.

sections.heading: Inner Line Permits (foreign visitors)
sections.text: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Kinnaur and Spiti near the Tibet border. Permits are issued at Himachal Bhawan in New Delhi, at the Deputy Commissioner's office in Shimla and Reckong Peo, and at SDM offices in Kalpa, Kaza and Manali.

guides.summary: What the July–September rains change in Himachal — landslide-prone roads, closed adventure sports — and where the season shines: dry Spiti and Lahaul, waterfalls and the Minjar fair.
guides.seoTitle: Himachal in the Monsoon: Roads, Spiti and Waterfalls
guides.seoDescription: Travelling in Himachal from July to September: landslides and road safety, the 15 July–15 September adventure closure, dry Spiti and Lahaul, waterfalls and monsoon fairs.

body.intro: The monsoon turns Himachal's lower valleys green and fills its waterfalls, but it also brings the year's worst roads. Plan around it rather than through it: here is what changes and where to go instead.

sections.heading: Where it stays dry: Spiti and Lahaul
sections.text: Spiti and Lahaul sit in the rain shadow and are cold and almost rainless. This is their season: buses run from Shimla via Kinnaur from May to October and from Manali from July to October, and Kaza's Ladarcha trade fair is held in July/August.

sections.text: Keep a spare day on any long road journey, travel in daylight and avoid planning rafting or paragliding between mid-July and mid-September. If you want the mountains without the rain, go to Spiti and Lahaul.

body.intro: Snow is the main reason many people come to Himachal in winter. It falls at different times in different places, and the highest roads close, so match the place to the month.

sections.heading: Roads in winter
sections.text: Heavy snow closes Rohtang Pass in late November and it reopens around May. The Atal Tunnel keeps Lahaul reachable from Manali, and Sissu is about 40 km away — but check locally, as its panchayat has at times paused tourist activities. Spiti can fall to −20°C in winter.

sections.heading: Stay safe
sections.text: Mountain weather changes fast, so carry woollens even on a sunny day, drive slowly on hill roads and use only licensed operators for skiing.
